title: The Interview Invite
intro: An email from a company invites you to an interview. You are wary, and rightly careful.
But some messages are real. Mirage loves it when you stop trusting the honest ones.

p.text: applying for Content Editor through our website

p: , on our company video link, with

p.text: two members of the editing team
There is no fee for any stage. We will never ask for your bank details before you are hired.

foot.text: The role is listed at craftloop.example/jobs.

addr.label: The company's real address
addr.lens: It comes from the company's own domain.
addr.why: A matching domain is good evidence.

applied.label: You did apply
applied.lens: It names the role you applied for.

when.label: A clear time and link
when.lens: A day, a time and a company video link.

who.label: Named interviewers
who.lens: You will meet two members of the team.

nopay.label: No fees, no bank details
nopay.lens: It says it never asks for money or bank details.

site.label: The role is listed on the site
site.lens: You can check the job page.

actions.label: Check the role on the company's jobs page, then attend the interview

go_ahead.line: The job was listed on the company's own page. The interview went well, and nobody asked for money or bank details.

ignore.line: Nothing bad happened. But a real interview invitation unanswered is a lost chance.

block_report.line: That was a real invitation. When every message looks like a scam, you can lose a real chance.
block_report.mirageSays: If you trust nothing, I win anyway.

what_if.block_report: You applied, it gave a time, named the interviewers, asked for no money and the role was on the jobs page. That is how real hiring looks.
what_if.ignore: Ignoring was safe. Recognising a real message is the skill: it asks for nothing secret and matches something you know.

golden_rule: A real interview invite follows something you did, is specific, and asks for no money or bank details.

quick_check.q: What made this interview invitation honest?

options.text: You had applied, it was specific and it asked for no money or bank details

quick_check.explain: Following your application, a clear plan and no payment are the real signs.

hints.nudge: What is this message actually asking you to do?

rows.k: Do honest employers ask for bank details before hiring?

rows.v: Look on the company's own jobs page
